edbDesc: A droplet of liquid surrounded by a thin film of gas, as opposed to a gas bubble, which is a sphere of gas surrounded by a thin film of liquid. Antibubbles are formed when liquid drops or flows turbulently into the same or another liquid. They can either skim across the surface of a liquid such as water (e.g. water globules), or be completely submerged in the liquid to which they are directed.
title: Antibubble
pickWhy: A fragile curiosity that lasts seconds to minutes, with no job at a useful size.
